faults.fault: The camera faces sideways out of the cutaway toward the viewer, not toward the dome membrane it must image; text says an inward-facing fisheye looking at the inner membrane.
A threaded stud runs up through the centre of the gel dome, which would block the camera's view of the membrane and pin the skin at its centre; nothing in the text calls for it.
Dome 'deforms over a rigid core' that is an SLA part while the camera must see the membrane from inside; the optical path through the core (clear window/support) is not described.
Incipient-slip flag '<10 ms' from marker divergence, but the camera runs at 60 fps (16.7 ms per frame); only the vibration channel could meet it.
Hertz indentation re-derives (24 um, contact radius 0.44 mm) but detectability is argued by precedent only; no signal-versus-noise estimate. Half-space Hertz applied to a 1.5 mm shell over a core.
Mass ~12 g, 5% force accuracy, 0.3 mm location stated without any budget or calculation.
A flesh-coloured skin-like strip appears behind the dome, not a described part.

C1.why: Fingertip-shaped 16 x 24 mm capsule on a robot finger; 1 mN supported by a correct Hertz estimate and vision-tactile precedent, not by a noise budget.

C2.why: Vision-based tactile plus vibration channel is a proven principle (GelSight/DIGIT class) and would work for location, force and slip.

C3.why: Hertz and dynamic-range numbers re-derive, but mass, accuracy and slip timing are unsupported and the 10 ms marker-based slip flag contradicts 60 fps.

C4.why: Shape and RGB lighting match, but the camera points the wrong way and the inset shows a stud through the dome.

C5.why: Buildable from catalogue parts; risks (abrasion, heating, creep, latency) are frank.

C6.why: Clear explanation of shading, marker flow and vibration paths for where, how hard and slip.

C7.why: Four concrete making steps with materials, thickness and calibration procedure.

C8.why: Two major generator errors (camera orientation, stud through dome) and a stray skin-coloured strip.

faults.fault: Hertz spread given as 1.47 mm; the stated formula with F=1 mN, R=8 mm, E*=0.3 MPa gives contact radius 0.27 mm (diameter 0.54 mm). The 1.47 mm figure is what justifies spreading 1 mN over 2-4 taxels for centroid location.

faults.fault: Claims 15.5 um sag 'well below 5 um'; 15.5 > 5, the own recomputation in the same line gives 384 um and prints 'Requirement <5um met? False', and the stated inputs actually give 1.8 um. The check contradicts itself.

faults.fault: Slip path needs 1-2 kHz sampling, but readout is '2x AD7746-class CDC'; an AD7746 converts at under ~91 Hz with two channels, far short of 19 (text) or ~100 (figure) taxels at kHz rates.

1.5 g total omits the CNC aluminium dovetail carrier and screws listed in the making steps.

faults.fault: M1.6 screw capacity uses 8 mm2 (tensile area ~1.27 mm2); margin is overstated (still large).
Risks section is empty.
Says 'Cast' a carrier that is CNC-milled.

C1.why: 1 mN capacitance budget is order-of-magnitude plausible, but the flat square stack is not fingertip-shaped and the slip requirement is not met by the named converter.

C2.why: Capacitive taxels can work, but as drawn the electrode gap does not change and slip sampling cannot reach the stated rate.

C3.why: Several numbers do not follow from their own inputs (Hertz spread, plate sag) and one constraint check contradicts its own printed result.

C4.why: Exploded stack is readable, but it is mounted on a human finger and the drawn electrode arrangement contradicts the mechanism.

C8.why: Clean exploded render, but the device sits on a human finger via a stray cube.

faults.fault: 3.57 fF applies the Hertz peak pressure (5.78 kPa on a 0.47 mm spot) to the whole 1.5 mm taxel. The mean pressure over the taxel is 0.44 kPa, giving ~0.27 fF, about 1 LSB at the stated 244 aF; a bonded 200 um silicone dielectric is also much stiffer in compression than p/E assumes. The 1 mN constraint is not shown.
The 43.2 ms micro-to-gross slip gap comes from a toy simulation with an arbitrary shear ramp (1.4 N over 150 ms); the deciding detector window rests on it.

Text: 20 mm dome on a nail-backed core with taxels on flat facets and the board dorsal. Figure: one flat tile on top of a faceted cup with the readout board sticking out sideways; against the 10 mm bar the core is ~25 mm wide and the assembly ~33 mm; not fingertip-shaped.
Gel interlayer drawn as a thick clear outer cup around the dome rather than a thin layer between skin and films.
Core drawn as a polyhedral ball on a screw, unlike the cup-shaped core in the main view.
50 N full scale gives 49% dielectric strain, called 'without saturation'.
Prints E_MPa 0.435 (3mu) while E*=0.58 MPa is used for contact; strain uses 435 kPa. Labelling inconsistency.

C1.why: Size near a fingertip in text, but the 1 mN check is overstated by ~13x and the drawn shape is not fingertip-like.

C2.why: Capacitive plus vibration-film dual path is sound in principle; light-touch sensitivity is marginal once corrected.

C3.why: Most arithmetic re-derives, but the deciding 1 mN signal and slip gap are wrong or unsupported.

C4.why: Shows dome, gel, grid, film and board, but the shape and board placement contradict the text.

C5.why: Buildable; risks listed with tests, but sensitivity is claimed as met when it is marginal.

'Steel post clamp and post' vs 'Clamped 6061-T6 tube' aluminium post.

Hold margin 1.11 against the high parked-torque estimate; parked aero torque is assumed, not derived.
Generator drawn as a brushed-motor can, not an outrunner; only two of four making steps illustrated.

C3.why: Power, rpm, voltage, thrust, moment, deflection, KE and disc temperature all re-derive; post I value wrong but conservative.

C4.why: Picture shows four blades and a turbine far longer than the cube, contradicting the text.

faults.fault: Four blades and four pitch grips at the hub; text specifies three blades on a 3-pin pitch hub.
'>4x margin' for blades and shaft at 22 m/s is only claimed; thrust is computed but no stress or deflection is.

faults.fault: Viscous dampers drawn as inclined struts from the deck steel to the outside of the TMD frame, which is itself bolted to the deck; as drawn they act across a rigid connection, not on the moving mass.
The deck slab shows a broken, notched dip with spalled edges, which reads as damage rather than the bending mode.
Bare 2.0 m/s2 and retrofitted 0.3 m/s2 are not derived from any stated crowd load; only the Q ratio is argued.
Deck mass 1.1 t/m for a deck drawn with a concrete slab (a 0.2 m x 3 m slab alone is ~1.4 t/m); modal mass, and hence mass ratio, may be off.
Empty citation placeholders (' .') after several precedent claims.
Odd built-up cruciform girder joints.

C3.why: Tuning, stiffness, damping, sag and stroke re-derive, but the comfort numbers have no stated forcing.

C4.why: Two spring-mass units under the deck are clear, but the damper connection contradicts the mechanism.

C5.why: Buildable with standard parts; risks of detuning, stroke and wear frankly listed.
